idioms.meaning_en: To be shocked into reality. Islahi writes: “This is an idiom, and it is usually interpreted to mean “to be embarrassed/ashamed.” Since however, a necessary result of embarrassment is to realize one’s mistake, it would not be wrong to render the idiom as to “realize/be warned.” To be on one’s guard take precautions, safeguard one’s position as a verb with an object In comparison to the expression in 4:71, this expression implies the taking of precautionary measures in any given situation.
